_comment: Which model runs which phase, by tier — the one place to turn. Read by scripts/process/dispatch.py; measured by process_kpis.py models (telemetry module). Phases: plan, execute, review. A tier without an entry falls back to `default` per phase. `command` is the project's way to start a worker session (the default is Claude Code's CLI; with another harness, put its CLI here): {model} and {prompt} are substituted inside the argv this template splits into; the prompt is one argv element; {branch} and {issue} name the session where the harness labels sessions (Claude Code: `--remote-control={branch}` makes each worker visible in the Claude app — the `=` form, because the flag's optional name would otherwise eat the prompt). TRUST: this command runs on the machine that runs dispatch — a change here is a change to what the steward's host executes; review it like CI configuration. `max_workers` caps concurrent dispatched sessions on this host. `runner`: `detached` (headless; a `-p` session needs its tool permissions granted in the project's settings or via --permission-mode, else it stops at the first gate) or `tmux` (each worker a window of tmux session `tmux_session` — interactive, a human can open it and `dispatch.py say` can type into it; use a non -p command then, e.g. `claude --model {model} --permission-mode acceptEdits {prompt}`; a fresh worktree may show a trust dialog on first start). `phases`: per-phase overrides — `{"review": {"command": "...", "runner": "detached", "remote": true}}`; `remote: true` means the session runs on another host (a cloud session, another machine): dispatch creates no worktree here, the command is the hand-over (it must exit 0 once the session is started; its stdout is kept), the branch must be on origin, and the worker reports with `--sync` so `tower.py --remote` sees it. Reviews are the natural remote phase: git-only, CPU-heavy, and a fresh clone on another host is independence for free.
